header.title: pKairo CG 51189 (pJuja): AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Book of the Dead
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:egy:tla:tb:pkairo-cg-51189-pjuja:translit, from the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (2018), in Simon Schweitzer's AED-TEI (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.63A.7: 63A.7: Babay (Bꜣbꜣy), perhaps the god Babi. 63A.8 seems incomplete; jwd 'separate' is a guess. 64.1: rn.w 'names' may stand for rʾ.w 'spells'. 64.3: sf, bkꜣ 'yesterday, morning'; ḥmw 'steering-oar'. 64.4: m n-sw.du is obscure. Much of 64.7-64.34 is obscure and translated tentatively: 64.7: mꜣꜣ.tn=j is the relative form, 'what I have seen'; 64.10 rʾ-6 is the fraction 1/6, or 'six spells'; 64.14 nzp,w unidentified; 64.16 ḥnti̯ perhaps for ḫnti 'go forward'; 64.21 nsq perhaps 'bite'; 64.22 jwr,t 'pregnant one'; 64.25 ḏꜣr,t perhaps 'scorpion', zmꜣ,yt.du unclear; 64.31 ḥnn,t unclear; 64.34 mr 'canal' or 'pyramid'. 64.19: Igeret is a name of the necropolis. 64.33: the Weary-hearted is Osiris. 64.41: the One in the Henu-bark is Sokar; the king Qenti (Qn,tj) is unidentified.
notes.125.1: Mꜣꜥ,tj, 'the Two Truths', is the dual of Maat. zꜣw,t ḏw,tjw, 'guarding of evildoers', sense uncertain. Wennefer is an epithet of Osiris.
notes.17.112: Mehet-weret (Mḥ,t-wr,t), 'Great Flood', is the celestial cow. wḏꜣ,t is the 'sound' eye.
notes.30B.1: jb and ḥꜣtj are two words for the heart; both are given as 'heart'. zp-2 marks 'my heart of my mother' as repeated.
notes.125.40: zp-4 marks 'I am pure' as said four times. Peret is the season of Emergence. ꜥrq,y is the last day of the month.
notes.125.47: The judges' names are translated where their sense is clear and kept as names where it is not (Serkheru, Sekhery, Temsep, Ihy, Tjenemy, Deny, Djudju, Wamemti, Shedkheru). Kheraha, Wenzi, Nedjfet, Wenet, Tjebu, Heqa-andj, Imet and Weryt are kept as written. Uncertain words: dbḥ (125.52), knj (125.57), ḥnwyt (125.59), ḥnb,t (125.61), ṯrm 'wink' (125.63), ṯpḥ,t ḏꜣi̯.t and nwḥ (125.64), ꜥm-jb, lit. 'swallow the heart' (125.66), jꜥi̯ (125.70), rhn (125.74), smt (125.76), šm rʾ (125.77), n-js (125.78), dꜣdꜣ (125.80), ḥr,w (125.81). 125.65 has no address in this copy; nkk is the passive partner. 125.66: ṯni̯ is marked corrupt.
notes.125.99: 125.105: ꜥw[,t] is uncertain, perhaps for ꜥwꜣ 'robbery'. 125.107: 'him' is not named.
notes.125.168: ḥpt.pl (here 'jambs') and zꜣwt (here 'floor') are parts of the gate; both uncertain. nḫn.w 'young ones, children'.
notes.125.183: The Interpreter (ꜥw) of the Two Lands is a title of Thoth. 125.192: hꜣ,yt 'roof' or 'portal'; what 'its' (=s, feminine) refers to is not stated.
notes.125.202: jḥ wꜣḏ: wꜣḏ 'green, fresh' may be a separate item (greens) or describe the cattle. ztj: yellow ochre. mꜣj 'lion' is unexpected here and may be corrupt. šns and psn are kinds of bread; ds is a jug. mḥ-jb, lit. 'one who fills the heart': a confidant.
notes.149.116: 149.116: kꜣ may be 'ka' or 'bull'; sḏḥ unidentified; ṯz-pẖr 'and vice versa'. 149.117: ḫwi̯ 'protect, ward off', or 'strike'; sense uncertain. 149.120 is obscure, perhaps the name or description of the Mound (mnḫ,t 'excellent', qꜣi̯ 'high', hꜣi̯ 'descend', ḥtp 'rest, peace').

nodes.text: As for Mehet-weret, it is the Wedjat-eye of Ra.
My heart of my mother, my heart of my mother! My heart of my forms! Do not stand against me as a witness,
do not oppose me in the tribunal,
do not show your enmity to me in the presence of the keeper of the balance.
I am Babay, the eldest son of Osiris, for whom every god gathered within his Eye in Heliopolis.
I am the one who separates(?); I am
Spell for knowing the names(?) of going forth, in a single spell.
Words spoken by [...], justified.

I am Yesterday and Tomorrow, who is over his births at another time, secret of *ba* (soul), who made the gods, who gives offerings to the Westerners, the western one of the sky, the steering-oar of the east, lord of faces, whose rays are seen, lord of uplifting, who comes forth from the twilight.
O his two falcons, who are over their council, who hear matters as the two kings(?): the foreleg is tied to the neck, the rump to the head!
O Westerner, give me those who are mine!
Great one of the two great ones(?), do not strike at me!
I weep at what I have seen.
I know the depths by your name, which was made for the needs of the *akhs* (transfigured spirits).
It is four millions, it is four hundred-thousands, at 1200 to it, at 30 cubits, in passing the united ones(?), in giving one by one there.
It is one sixth(?), the portion of the Foremost of the Duat, the hour of felling the rebel.
I have come from there justified.
This is the portion of the one who is in the forecourt of the Duat: seven strides in his going forth.
It is my protection, as the safeguard of his spells(?).
The blood is cool, the *nzpw* are fresh(?).
I have parted the two horns(?) in my union(?).
Come forward(?) to me in secret.
I create through my repelling(?).
Those who are on their bellies: let me swallow the eye; it weeps(?).
Igeret, open the sealed door(?) to me!
May you give me a good way, that I may pass.
Who are you, then, the biter(?) in the West?
I am the pregnant one(?).
I have laid down the burden.
Sealed is the back(?) upon the wall.
It is the overturned *ḏꜣrt*, fallen on the back of the Benu, on the two *zmꜣyt*.
Horus has removed his eye for him.
His face is bright at the dawning of the land.
My name is his name.
I do not perish.
I come into being as a lion.
The *ḥnnt* of Shu is in me.
I am one whom he does not seize(?).
How fine is the mooring of the Weary-hearted!
He makes a landing by the canal(?).
Behold, I go forth.
I am the Lord of Life.
Going forth by day; not turning a man back on the road of the Duat, in entering, in going forth; taking forms as anything his heart [desires].
It is a man's not dying again.
As for one who knows this spell, it is his justification on earth.
He does everything that the living do.
This spell was found in the foundations of the One in the Henu-bark by the overseer of builders of the wall, in the time of the King of Upper and Lower Egypt Qenti.
This secret procedure is not seen, not looked upon.
This spell is to be recited by one pure and clean, who does not approach women, who does not eat small cattle or fish.
Spell for going forth by day.
Words spoken by [...], justified, before the great god.
What is to be said on reaching the Hall of the Two Truths, to see the faces of the gods.
Words spoken by [...], justified.
Hail to you, great god, lord of the Two Truths!
I have come to you to see your beauty.

I know you, I know your name, I know the names of the 42 gods who are with you in the Hall of the Two Truths, who live on the guarding of evildoers, who swallow their blood on that day of reckoning characters in the presence of Wennefer.
I have not turned back a god [in] his procession.
I am pure! Four times.
My purity is the purity of that great Benu who is in Herakleopolis,
for I am that nose of the Lord of Breath who makes all the people live, on that day of filling the Wedjat-eye, in the second month of Peret, on the last day, in the presence of the lord of this land.
I am one who saw the filling of the Wedjat-eye in Heliopolis.
O Wide-of-Stride, who came forth from Heliopolis, I have not done wrong.
O Embracer-of-Fire, who came forth from Kheraha, I have not robbed.
O Nose, who came forth from Hermopolis, I have not been covetous.
O Swallower-of-Shadows, who came forth from the cavern, I have not stolen.
O Terrible-of-Face, who came forth from Rosetau, I have not killed people.
O Double Lion, who came forth from the sky, I have not damaged the offering-measure(?).
O His-Eyes-are-Fire, who came forth from Letopolis, I have not done crookedness.
O Flame, who came forth going backwards, I have not stolen god's property.
O Bone-Breaker, who came forth from Herakleopolis, I have not told lies.
O Commander-of-Flame, who came forth from Memphis, I have not taken [things] away by force.
O Cavern-Dweller, who came forth from the West, I have not been sullen(?).
O White-of-Teeth, who came forth from the Fayum, I have not transgressed.
O Blood-Eater, who came forth from the slaughterhouse, I have not done *ḥnwyt*.
O Entrail-Eater, who came forth from the slaughterhouse, I have not slaughtered divine cattle.
O Lord of Maat, who came forth from the Two Truths, I have not robbed the measured fields(?).
O Serkheru, who came forth from Wenzi, I have not caused disturbance.
O Bastite, who came forth from the secret place, I have not winked(?).
O He-whose-Face-is-Behind-Him, who came forth from the cavern of crossing(?), I have not done *nwḥ*.
I have not copulated with a catamite.
O Raised-of-Foot(?), who came forth from the twilight, I have not been secretive(?).
O Dark One, who came forth from the darkness, I have not reviled.
O Bringer-of-his-Offering, who came forth from Sais, I have not been violent.
O Lord of Faces, who came forth from Nedjfet, I have not been hasty of heart.
O Sekhery, who came forth from Wenet, I have not reviled the god's washing(?).
O Lord of Lords(?), who came forth from Sais, I have not been talkative in speech.
O Nefertem, who came forth from Memphis, there is no wrongdoing of mine, I have not done evil.
O Temsep, who came forth from Busiris, I have not cursed the king.
O Who-Acts-by-his-Will, who came forth from Tjebu, I have not waded(?) in the water.
O Ihy, who came forth from Nun, my voice has not been loud.
O Tjenemy, who came forth from Bubastis, I have not eavesdropped(?).
O Deny, who came forth from Heliopolis, my mouth has not run on(?).
O Djudju, who came forth from Heqa-andj, I have not quarrelled except over my own property(?).
O Wamemti, who came forth from the place of execution, I have not copulated with a married woman.
O Bringer-of-his-Offering, who came forth from the house of Min, I have not fornicated(?).
O Chief of the Great Ones, who came forth from Imet, I have not caused terror(?).
O Destroyer, who came forth from Xois, I have not transgressed.
O Shedkheru, who came forth from Weryt, I have not been hot-tempered.
No misdeed of mine has come before the king of his day.
Hail to you who are in the [Hall] of the Two Truths, who have no lie in their bodies, who live on Maat, who feed on Maat in the presence of Horus who is in his disk!
Rescue me from Babi, who lives on the entrails of the great ones on that day of the great reckoning.
Behold, I have come to you;
there is no wrongdoing of mine,
there is no crime of mine,
there is no robbery(?) of mine,
there is no witness against me,
there is nothing I have done against him.
I live on Maat,
my heart feeds on Maat.
I have done what people say and what the gods are content with.
I have satisfied the god with what he loves.
I have given bread to the hungry, water to the thirsty, clothes to the naked.
I have given god's offerings to the gods and invocation-offerings to the *akhs* (transfigured spirits).
So rescue me!
'Breast of Shu, which he gave as protection for Osiris' is your name.
'We will not let you enter past us,' say the jambs(?) of this gate, 'unless you say our names.'
'Children of the Uraei' it is.
You know us;
pass by us, then.
'I will not let you enter past me,' says the floor(?) of this gate, 'unless you say my name.'
Tell it to the Interpreter of the Two Lands.
Who is he?
The Interpreter of the Two Lands is Thoth.
Why have you come?
I have come to be reported.
What is your condition?
I am pure of wrongs, of the abuse of those who are in their day;
I have not put myself in their hands.
To whom shall I report you?
The roof is of fire, its walls are of uraei, and the floor of its house is of water.
Who is that?
It is Osiris.
Proceed, then!
Behold, you are reported.
This spell is to be said [by one] pure and clean, clothed in his garments, shod in white sandals, anointed with myrrh, having offered cattle, greens(?), fowl, incense, bread, beer and vegetables.
And you shall make this image, which is in writing, in ochre, laid out on ground on which no *mꜣj* at all has trodden.
As for one for whom this book is made, he will flourish,
his children will flourish,
he will be a confidant of the king and of his court.
There will be given to him *šns*-bread, a *ds*-jug, *psn*-bread and a large portion of meat on the altar of the great god.
He will not be turned back at any gate of the West.
He will be ushered in with the kings of Upper and Lower Egypt.
He will be a confidant of Osiris.
Truly effective, a million times.
His *ka* (vital force) falls to the *sḏḥ*, and vice versa.
You shall ward off for me(?).
Your head is cut off by Mafdet.
The eighth Mound.
Excellent, high; descending in peace(?).
